report.tagline: The real-time public conversation app formerly called Twitter, now owned by SpaceX through xAI and built around Grok AI.
report.simpleSummary: X is the app once called Twitter, where people post short messages, follow news as it happens and argue in public. Elon Musk bought it in 2022 for $44 billion, renamed it X, cut most staff, and changed how it works: blue ticks are now paid, fact-checks come from users through Community Notes, and the Grok AI chatbot is built in. It makes money from ads and subscriptions, but ad income has fallen sharply since Twitter days.

overview.whatItDoes: X is a public social network for short posts, news, live events and debate. Users follow accounts, see a For You feed ranked by AI, and can watch video, join Spaces audio chats and ask Grok questions. Since March 2025 X has been part of xAI, and since early 2026 part of SpaceX.
howItWorks: Users post text, images and video, and reply, repost and like.
The For You feed ranks posts using an algorithm that now leans on Grok AI; a Following feed shows only accounts you follow.
Verification blue ticks come with X Premium, a paid subscription, rather than identity checks for public figures.
Community Notes lets users add context to misleading posts, shown when people with different views agree.
X earns from ads, subscriptions and data licensing, and creators earn a share of ad revenue on their replies.
overview.valueProposition: The fastest place to see what is happening right now and hear directly from public figures, with an AI assistant built in.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Shows posts from followed and recommended accounts.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Core experience; ranking decides what millions see.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Paid tiers give a blue tick, reply boost, longer posts and fewer ads.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: New revenue, but the EU fined X €120 million for making the tick misleading.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Users write notes on posts; notes appear when raters with different views agree.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Scales fact-checking cheaply; Meta later copied the idea.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: xAI's chatbot inside X, used by about 117 million people monthly.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: A reason to stay in X and to pay for subscriptions, but also a source of scandals like image deepfakes.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Pays Premium creators a share of ad revenue from replies to their posts.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Keeps posters active, but can reward rage bait.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Payments inside X, in beta since November 2025.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Part of the 'everything app' plan; delayed by regulators.

steps.detail: Sees a Community Note on a misleading video.
Asks Grok to summarise what is known.
App suggests Premium to boost replies.
Receives a payout every two weeks if eligible.
Checks for ads next to harmful content.

businessModel.summary: X earns most of its money from ads, plus subscriptions and data licensing. Ad revenue fell from Twitter's roughly $4.5 billion a year to $1.8 billion in 2025 as many big brands left. Subscriptions are growing but small.

revenueStreams.detail: Timeline and video ads; $1.8 billion in 2025.
About 4.4 million paid subscribers; X and Grok subscriptions grew by $365 million in 2025.
Companies pay for access to X posts and the API.
Grok subscriptions and xAI revenue sit in the wider group.

businessModel.pricing: Free for users. X Premium has Basic, Premium and Premium+ tiers; in India Premium is roughly ₹400 to ₹600 a month, varying by platform and changes.
costDrivers: Servers and AI, now shared with xAI
Engineering staff, much smaller since 2022 layoffs
Interest on debt from the 2022 buyout
businessModel.unitEconomics: Rough estimate. $1.8 billion of ad revenue spread over about 550 million monthly users is about $3.30 per user a year, far below Meta. Each Premium subscriber may pay about $50 to $100 a year, but only about 4.4 million pay. X cut costs by laying off most staff, so it may run close to break-even before debt costs, but it is earning much less per user than Twitter once did.

howTheyGetUsers: Famous people, including Musk himself, posting first on X
Embedded posts on news sites and TV
growth.moat: X still has the habit of being 'where news breaks', with many politicians, journalists and celebrities posting there first. That network is hard to move. But Threads now has more mobile daily users, so the moat is shrinking.

competitors.name: ChatGPT and Gemini

northStar.metric: Daily active users who read or join a real-time conversation
northStar.why: X's value is real-time conversation. This north star tracks people who come to see what is happening and take part, which drives ad views and subscriptions.

children.description: Share of viral misleading posts with a note.

strengths: Still the place where much news breaks first
Community Notes is a widely praised idea
Grok gives a built-in AI with live data
weaknesses: Ad revenue down to $1.8 billion from Twitter's much higher level
Paid ticks reduced trust in verification
Product decisions depend heavily on one owner
risks: EU Digital Services Act fines and other regulation
Grok scandals over deepfake images, investigated in the UK, EU, India and elsewhere
userComplaints: Paid accounts pushed to the top of replies
Algorithm showing posts users did not ask for

improvementIdeas.idea: Separate identity verification badge from paid Premium
improvementIdeas.problem: Users and the EU say paid ticks are misleading.

improvementIdeas.idea: Rank replies by quality, not just Premium
improvementIdeas.problem: Low-quality paid replies crowd out real ones.

improvementIdeas.idea: Faster Community Notes on viral posts using AI drafts reviewed by humans
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Time to first note on viral posts

improvementIdeas.idea: Brand safety guarantees with third-party verification

pmLessons: Trust is part of the product. Selling verification made the blue tick less useful.
Cost cuts can keep a company alive, but revenue depends on users and advertisers trusting the platform.
Crowd-sourced ideas like Community Notes can scale where paid teams cannot.
Adding AI like Grok brings new users but also new risks.

interviewQuestions.question: Was making verification paid a good product decision?
interviewQuestions.hint: Weigh subscription revenue against trust, impersonation and EU fines. Suggest a better design.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you bring advertisers back to X?
interviewQuestions.hint: Find why they left, propose safety tools and measurement, track advertiser count.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you measure if Community Notes works?
interviewQuestions.hint: Look at spread of noted posts, time to note, and agreement across viewpoints.

interviewQuestions.question: Threads passed X in mobile daily users. What should X do?
interviewQuestions.hint: Segment users, defend news and web strengths, improve new user retention.

interviewQuestions.question: What is X's north star?
interviewQuestions.hint: Daily users in real-time conversation, broken into users, health, posting and revenue.
